# FINAL COMPREHENSIVE REPORT: Nuclear Energy Mentions in 2023 IPCC Report (85-Page Version) ## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY **FINAL ANSWER: 1 page** The 2023 IPCC report (85-page version) mentions nuclear energy on exactly **1 page** (page 69). This finding is based on comprehensive analysis of the complete PDF document with exhaustive text searches across all content. --- ## DOCUMENT IDENTIFICATION ### The Correct Document The "85-page version" of the 2023 IPCC report refers to: **Official Title:** Climate Change 2023: Synthesis Report - Longer Report **Report Type:** IPCC AR6 Synthesis Report (Sixth Assessment Report) **Publication Date:** March 20, 2023 **Approval Date:** March 19, 2023 (IPCC 58th Session, Interlaken, Switzerland) **Publisher:** Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), Geneva, Switzerland **DOI:** 10.59327/IPCC/AR6-9789291691647 **Official PDF:** https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/syr/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_SYR_LongerReport.pdf ### Page Count Clarification - **Content pages:** 81 pages (pages 35-115 in the document citation) - **Commonly referenced as:** 85 pages (when including front matter/preliminary pages) - **Official IPCC reference:** "AR6 Longer Report ran to 80 pages" The discrepancy between 81 and 85 pages stems from whether front matter and cover pages are included. Multiple credible sources (French Wikipedia, Scientists for Extinction Rebellion, Rainforest Foundation) reference this as the "85-page" report. ### Context Within AR6 Synthesis Report The AR6 Synthesis Report was released in three versions: 1. **Summary for Policymakers (SPM):** 36 pages 2. **Longer Report:** 81/85 pages ← **THE DOCUMENT ANALYZED** 3. **Full Volume (SYR):** 184 pages --- ## METHODOLOGY ### Step 1: Document Identification (Completed) - Searched for "IPCC 2023 85 pages" and "IPCC AR6 Synthesis Report 2023" - Confirmed the document is the "Longer Report" component - Verified publication date and official download location - Cross-referenced multiple sources to ensure correct document identification ### Step 2: PDF Analysis and Text Search (Completed) - Downloaded the official PDF from IPCC website - Extracted text from all 81 pages using PyPDF2 library - Conducted comprehensive case-insensitive searches for: - "nuclear" (general term) - "nuclear energy" - "nuclear power" - "nuclear electricity" - "nuclear plant" - "nuclear reactor" - "atomic energy" - "atomic power" - Any word containing "nucl" pattern - Searched across all document elements: main text, footnotes, figure captions, tables, and references - Performed multiple verification passes to ensure completeness --- ## DETAILED FINDINGS ### Search Results Summary **Total occurrences of "nuclear" (any form):** 1 **Total unique pages containing "nuclear":** 1 **Page number:** 69 ### Complete Context of the Single Mention **Location:** Page 69 **Section:** Section 4 - "Near-Term Responses in a Changing Climate" **Figure Title:** "There are multiple opportunities for scaling up climate action" **Subsection:** Part (a) "Feasibility of climate responses and adaptation, and potential of mitigation options in the near term" **Category:** Energy Supply Mitigation Options **Exact Context (Direct Quote):** > "Reduce methane and N2O in agriculture Reduce food loss and food waste Geothermal and hydropower Carbon sequestration in agriculture Reduce conversion of natural ecosystems **Nuclear** Reduce methane from coal, oil and gas Bioelectricity (includes BECCS) Fossil Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) Ecosystem restoration, afforestation, reforestation" **Description:** The word "Nuclear" appears as a single label within a comprehensive figure/chart displaying various mitigation options organized by sector. It is listed among Energy Supply options alongside wind, solar, geothermal, hydropower, bioelectricity (includes BECCS), and fossil CCS. The figure presents these options with their: - Potential contribution to net emission reduction by 2030 (measured in GtCO₂-eq/yr) - Cost ranges (USD per tCO₂-eq) - Feasibility levels - Synergies with mitigation **Format:** "Nuclear" appears as a standalone label in a densely packed figure showing multiple climate mitigation strategies. ### What Was NOT Found - No dedicated textual discussion of nuclear energy - No analysis or elaboration about nuclear power - No mentions of "nuclear energy," "nuclear power," "nuclear electricity," "nuclear plant," or "nuclear reactor" as complete phrases - No references to nuclear in footnotes, tables, or bibliography sections - No discussion of nuclear's role in climate mitigation beyond its inclusion as a labeled option in the single figure --- ## KEY OBSERVATIONS 1. **Minimal Coverage:** Nuclear energy receives extremely limited attention in this synthesis report, appearing only as a labeled option in a single figure on page 69. 2. **No Substantive Discussion:** There is no narrative text discussing nuclear energy's role, benefits, challenges, or potential contribution to climate mitigation. 3. **Visual Representation Only:** The sole mention occurs in a visual chart/figure rather than in analytical text. 4. **Context of Mention:** Nuclear is acknowledged as one of many near-term mitigation options in the energy supply sector but is not given special emphasis or detailed treatment. 5. **Search Completeness:** Multiple comprehensive searches using different search patterns and methods confirmed this is definitively the only occurrence in the entire 81-page document. --- ## VERIFICATION SOURCES ### Primary Document Source - **Official IPCC Website:** https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/syr/ - **Direct PDF Link:** https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/syr/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_SYR_LongerReport.pdf ### Document Identification Sources - Scientists for Extinction Rebellion: "The Synthesis Report of the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) is 85 pages" - French Wikipedia (GIEC): "Beaucoup plus court que les autres rapports, il compte 85 pages" - Rainforest Foundation: "This 85-page report has been recognized as a 'final warning' to act on climate change" - Official IPCC AR7 scoping document: "AR6 Longer Report ran to 80 pages" ### Analysis Method - Direct PDF download and text extraction - Automated pattern matching and manual verification - Analysis date: January 9, 2026 --- ## ANSWER TO SPECIFIC QUESTION INTERPRETATIONS ### Interpretation 1: "How many pages mention nuclear energy?" **Answer:** 1 page (page 69) ### Interpretation 2: "How many times is nuclear mentioned?" **Answer:** 1 occurrence (though this was not the question asked) ### Interpretation 3: "Which pages contain nuclear-related terms?" **Answer:** Only page 69 contains any nuclear-related term --- ## CONCLUSION Based on exhaustive analysis of the IPCC AR6 Synthesis Report Longer Report (the 85-page version published March 2023), nuclear energy is mentioned on **exactly 1 page** (page 69). This mention occurs as a single label in a figure showing various mitigation options, with no accompanying textual discussion or analysis. The search methodology was comprehensive, covering all text elements across all 81 content pages, and multiple verification passes confirmed no additional mentions exist in the document. **FINAL ANSWER: 1 page**
